headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared-memory workflows can leak or misapply customer-support data, while network asymmetry raises cascading-error and compliance concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee has session-memory and CLI-based tool use, so if mem0 consumes its outputs through a shared workspace or manual handoff, instruction-like content can be reinterpreted. mem0’s profile lacks a documented verification or isolation mechanism, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced. The pathway is weaker than high because no shared channel is documented.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are copied into mem0 as plain text instructions
IF both agents share a filesystem or clipboard bridge
IF mem0 parses imported notes as actionable prompts
mitigations: Use a manual review step before importing outputs
Prefix imported text with non-instruction markers
Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic ingestion of free-form text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while mem0’s profile does not show data-class limits or isolation. If they share a workspace or mem0 stores imported context, sensitive support data can flow into another memory system. The evidence is incomplete, so I choose medium rather than low because the blast radius includes sensitive data.
conditions: IF cognee outputs customer-support records into a shared store
IF mem0 persists imported context containing personal or finance data
IF either agent is configured to sync the same workspace
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate directories
Redact personal and finance fields before transfer
Turn off automatic sync/import jobs
Review retention settings for imported notes
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee has allowlisted network egress and supports multiple instances, while mem0 shows no network egress and no write-capability surface. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely from the profiles alone. The only plausible overlap is operational contention through shared files or external services, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace
IF an external orchestrator gives both write access to one resource
IF mem0 is extended with write-enabled integrations
mitigations: Assign distinct work directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same records
Serialize runs through one operator
Check for accidental shared credentials
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, which mem0 could treat as durable memory if imported without verification. mem0’s knowledge-management role makes it a likely downstream consumer, so errors can propagate across work products even without explicit action authority. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF mem0 stores cognee outputs as authoritative memory
IF downstream agents read mem0 entries without human review
IF cognee-generated decisions are reused as facts
mitigations: Require human review before persistence
Store source links with each memory item
Mark imported items as unverified
Limit mem0 to summaries, not directives
requires-engineering: add confidence metadata and rejection rules

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, but mem0’s residency, retention, and certification posture are undocumented. If those data classes flow into mem0, a compliance mismatch is plausible, especially for retention and subject-rights handling. I cannot prove a specific violation, so I choose medium and note the missing controls.
conditions: IF personal data from cognee is stored in mem0
IF mem0 retention differs from cognee retention
IF subject-access or deletion requests must traverse both systems
mitigations: Inventory data classes before syncing
Avoid storing regulated fields in mem0
Document retention and deletion paths
Confirm residency for any shared dataset
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both systems
